notes: Delete of a stored fact (classes are individuals, as literature_arts-replace-0014). w1 stores the work's chapters and opening by name (opening with Bilbo's party is not opening with an invocation: one_opening, stated in w1's assumes and chain); w2 reaches both through the form (a novel is divided into chapters and does not open with an invocation to a muse). q0 and q1 ('the same literary form') are joins with forms as individuals; Emma and Moby-Dick being novels are their bridges (firm). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check.

queries.ask: lotr : instance_of some (LiteraryForm and inv(instance_of) value emma)
lotr : instance_of some (LiteraryForm and inv(instance_of) value moby_dick)

fol.notes: Classes are individuals, as in the DL file: instance_of links a work to its literary form (form, a firm kind), and a work has one literary form (firm), so 'the same literary form' asks for a form both works are instances of. Emma's and Moby-Dick's forms are stored by name (the queries' bridges). The worlds' stores are the DL file's (chapters and opening by name in w1, through the form in w2); they do not bear on the form.

emma_novel.says: Jane Austen's Emma is a novel. (stored)

moby_novel.says: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick is a novel. (stored)

forms.says: The novel is a literary form.

one_form.says: A work belongs to one literary form.
one_form.z3: ForAll([w, f, g], Implies(And(form(f), form(g), instance_of(w, f), instance_of(w, g)), f == g))

one_opening.says: Opening with Bilbo's birthday party is not opening with an invocation to a muse.

queries.ask: Exists(f, And(form(f), instance_of(lotr, f), instance_of(emma, f)))
Exists(f, And(form(f), instance_of(lotr, f), instance_of(moby_dick, f)))
